correctness.rationale: For row exponents (0,1,2,4), generalized Vandermonde equals ordinary Vandermonde times z1+z2+z3+z4. Distinct N-th roots ensure first factor nonzero. For four unit roots with sum zero, e1=0 and e3=e4 conjugate(e1)=0, so root polynomial Q(t)=t^4+e2 t²+e4 is even: roots occur in two antipodal pairs. Conversely antipodal pairs sum zero, possible among Nth roots precisely when N is even. Choose two of N/2 pairs gives binomial count; three consecutive rows give a rank-three Vandermonde, so singular rank exactly 3. Uniformity over divisors: even N fails mod2 occupancies (3,1), odd N has d=3 counts (1,2,1) or all distinct d>=5. Inspected full RESULT and exact cyclotomic/polynomial verification source; finite N<=40 confirms only, not proves all N.
